newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Roma gets Gippsland petroleum permit.
newsitem.headline: Roma gets Gippsland petroleum permit.

text.p: Roma Petroleum NL said on Wednesday it has been awarded a petroleum exploration permit over 1,889 square kilometres in Australia's onshore Gippsland Basin.
The permit area, called 137, is centered on the town of Seaspray in the state of Victoria, Roma exploration manager Roger Meaney said.
A number of wells in the permit area have encountered hydrocarbon shows, he said.
"We hope to start drilling later this year," he said.
Meaney said he did not anticipate that exploration will be hampered by the federal government's recent Wik decision because the land in the area is essentially freehold title.
The Wik decision ruled that leasehold title does not necessarily extinguish native land titles in Australia.
Roma earlier this year deferred some exploration programmes on and near the northern Cooper Basin in Queensland due to the Wik ruling.
